facts_of_case: Complainant filed a complaint against Sri Mahalingappa and others for bigamy; accused was acquitted but ordered to pay compensation of Rs. 10,000/-; present revision petition is filed against the order awarding compensation.

legal_principles.principle: The law declared by the Hon'ble Supreme Court shall be having binding effect on all Courts within the territory of India.
legal_principles.held: Under Article 141 of the Constitution, what is to be noted is that the law declared by the Hon'ble Supreme Court is binding on all the Courts within the territory of India.

legal_principles.principle: Decisions even of the highest Court on questions which are essentially questions of fact, cannot be cited as precedents governing the decision of other cases.
legal_principles.held: Decisions even of the highest Court on questions which are essentially questions of fact, cannot be cited as precedents governing the decision of other cases which must rest in the ultimate analysis upon their own particular facts.
cited_cases: PRAKASH CHANDRA V. STATE OF U.P., AIR 1969 SC 195

legal_principles.principle: What is binding as precedent is the principle underlying the decision.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down that what is binding as precedent is the principle underlying the decision.
cited_cases: PRAKASH AMICHAND SHAH V. STATE OF GUJARAT AND ORS.

legal_principles.principle: A decision is available as a precedent only if it decides a question of law.
legal_principles.held: In the case of STATE OF PUNJAB V. SURINDER KUMAR, that while considering the question of precedents the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as follows:— 'A decision is available as a precedent only if it decides a question of law'.
cited_cases: STATE OF PUNJAB V. SURINDER KUMAR

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and set aside the order awarding compensation.

use_for_drafting: defending against criminal action for bigamy
advising on Hindu marriage and divorce laws
